prompt: Finish a bounded first-in-first-out task queue backed by an ArrayList. Keep its invariants: never exceed the capacity, never store a blank task, and never crash when empty.
explanation: The backing ArrayList holds the tasks in arrival order, so adding at the end and removing from index 0 gives first-in-first-out behaviour. Every mutating method has to defend the invariants before it touches the list -- a rejected offer must leave the queue exactly as it was, and poll on an empty queue returns null instead of letting remove(0) throw. Clamping the capacity in the constructor means the rest of the class can simply trust the field.
hints: Add at the end of the list and remove from index 0 -- that pairing is what makes the queue first-in-first-out.
offer should check every reason to refuse (full, null, blank) BEFORE it adds anything, so a rejected task leaves the queue untouched.
poll and peek must test isEmpty() first and return null, otherwise get(0) on an empty ArrayList throws.
